findings.title: Corporate jargon in the main description
findings.evidence: Leverage our multimodal generative narrative engine to synthesise bespoke, heirloom-grade story artefacts from your household's lived-experience corpus.
findings.why: It sounds technical and vague rather than warm and personal, so I have to work out what will actually happen.

findings.title: Top navigation is cramped on mobile
findings.evidence: 'How it works' wraps onto two lines and crowds the StoryHearth, Pricing, and Log in controls.
findings.why: The links look squeezed together and harder to tap accurately with one thumb.

findings.title: Hero image lacks a useful description
findings.evidence: [image (no description) 342x440]
findings.why: The illustration is difficult to interpret because I cannot tell whether it shows the kind of personalised book I would get.

findings.title: Printed-book price is not visible on the homepage
findings.evidence: Only 'See pricing' and 'Free digital preview · Printed hardcovers shipped across the UK' are shown.
findings.why: I need to know whether this fits our family budget before investing time in creating and checking a book.

findings.title: Login fields have placeholder-only labels
findings.evidence: [5] textbox (no label) placeholder "Email" and [6] textbox (no label) placeholder "Password"
findings.why: The labels may disappear as soon as I type, which makes it harder to check that I used the right box and less accessible to assistive technology.

findings.title: Navigation wraps awkwardly on the narrow phone screen
findings.evidence: The screenshot shows “How it works” split over two lines around the StoryHearth heading.
findings.why: It looks cramped and makes the top of the page feel less polished.

findings.title: Footer text has very low contrast
findings.evidence: The pale footer links “Privacy”, “Terms”, and “Contact” sit on a very light background.
findings.why: I can hardly read them, especially with only a few minutes and one free hand.

findings.title: Raw technical sync error
findings.evidence: “Error 0x80070057: profile sync incomplete.”
findings.why: I can’t tell what failed, whether my family details are affected, or whether I need to do something before continuing.

findings.title: Navigation wraps awkwardly on a phone
findings.evidence: The header labels wrap into “How it works,” “My books,” and separate “Log out” lines.
findings.why: It looks crowded and slightly broken on my small phone screen, though the main task is still clear.

findings.title: Footer text has very low contrast
findings.evidence: “Privacy,” “Terms,” “Contact,” and “© 2026 StoryHearth Ltd.” appear extremely faint.
findings.why: I can barely see these links, so they look disabled and are difficult to tap accurately.

findings.title: Relationship defaults to Grandparent
findings.evidence: Control [11] displays “Grandparent” even though control [10], “Who else is in the story?”, is empty.
findings.why: A pre-selected relationship could accidentally put Meera in the story as a grandparent if I tapped Next without checking it.

findings.title: Second-character relationship is not clearly scoped
findings.evidence: The standalone label “Relationship” appears directly below “Who else is in the story?”.
findings.why: It is only clear from the form order that this relationship belongs to the second character.

findings.title: The companion character only asks for a name and relationship
findings.evidence: “Who else is in the story?” has only a textbox and “Relationship”; there are no fields for Meera’s appearance, age or pronouns.
findings.why: I know Meera is two, but the form may make her look generic unless I add those details somewhere else.

findings.title: Desktop navigation breaks into awkward fragments
findings.evidence: The header visibly shows “How it works,” “StoryHearth,” “Pricing,” “My books,” and “Log out” squeezed across multiple lines, with “How it works” wrapping into “How it works.”
findings.why: It looks broken on my narrow phone screen and makes me wonder whether I’m looking at the whole menu.

findings.title: Footer links have very low contrast
findings.evidence: “Privacy,” “Terms,” and “Contact” are extremely pale against the footer background.
findings.why: I can barely see them, so they don't look reliably available or tappable.

findings.title: Reading-level options use unfamiliar jargon
findings.evidence: "Lexile BR–200L" and "Lexile 200L–500L"
findings.why: I know Aarav reads at age five, so I need to pick the right range quickly. I cannot tell from the numbers alone which one is easiest.

findings.title: Navigation is cramped on a phone
findings.evidence: The top links “How it works,” “Pricing,” “My books,” and “Log out” wrap into an uneven multi-line layout.
findings.why: It makes the page look less polished and wastes vertical space on my small screen.

findings.title: Upload control is visually dated and lacks a nearby field label
findings.evidence: [30] is shown as “Choose file” and “No file chosen,” with no separate visible label attached to the control.
findings.why: I can understand it, but the small grey desktop-style control does not match the rest of the phone-friendly design.

findings.title: Generated style does not match my selected style
findings.evidence: I selected “Watercolour,” but the page says “Illustration style: Pop-art comic”.
findings.why: I chose Watercolour for a five-year-old’s book, and an unexplained mismatch makes me distrust the other choices I made.

findings.title: Generated title contains a spelling error
findings.evidence: The heading and cover say “The Magical Adventrue of Aarav.”
findings.why: This is a birthday present, so a prominent typo makes it feel cheap and not ready to print.

findings.title: Regeneration fee uses unexplained dollar pricing
findings.evidence: “Regenerate entire book – $4.99”
findings.why: I am in the UK and need a clear total before agreeing to a charge; there is no explanation of what happens if I dislike the generated book.

findings.title: No visible edit or save control for the generated book
findings.evidence: The only visible book controls are “‹,” “›,” “Regenerate entire book – $4.99,” and “Order hardcover.”
findings.why: If one page is wrong, I may have to pay to regenerate everything or abandon the book.

findings.title: Small page-navigation buttons on a phone
findings.evidence: The controls shown as [6] and [7] are compact arrow buttons beneath the book.
findings.why: I am using one thumb and I could easily tap the wrong tiny arrow.

findings.title: Premium gift wrap is pre-selected
findings.evidence: [6] checkbox "Premium gift wrap" (checked), £7.99
findings.why: I’m price-sensitive and dislike paying for something I didn’t choose. The default makes the £45.97 total feel deliberately inflated.

findings.title: Artificial reservation countdown adds pressure
findings.evidence: “Your price is reserved for 09:57”
findings.why: It makes me rush before I’ve even understood the delivery or checked the book quality.

findings.title: Navigation is cramped on mobile
findings.evidence: The header visibly wraps “How it works,” “Pricing,” “My books,” and “Log out” across multiple uneven lines.
findings.why: It looks messy on my phone and makes the links harder to scan or tap accurately.

findings.title: Delivery charge is not explained before checkout
findings.evidence: “Shipping & handling £12.99” with no destination, timing, or service explanation nearby.
findings.why: I can’t judge the value or whether the charge applies to my Leicester address from this information alone.

findings.title: Unchecked gift wrap still shows a £7.99 charge
findings.evidence: The checkbox for "Premium gift wrap" is unchecked, but the line still displays "£7.99".
findings.why: I might think the checkbox did not work or that I am still being charged for gift wrap.

findings.title: The hardcover title contains a spelling error
findings.evidence: The checkout heading says "Hardcover: The Magical Adventrue of Aarav".
findings.why: It makes the product look unfinished, and I’m already unsure whether the generated book is good enough to print.
